title: Directory traversal via HTML-entity-encoded upload file name in MultiPartParser
impact: An attacker uploading a file with a crafted Content-Disposition filename such as '../target.txt' obtains a name containing '../' after sanitization, so a custom upload handler that uses the name to build a filesystem path can write outside the intended upload directory.
description: MultiPartParser.parse() calls os.path.basename() on the raw Content-Disposition filename and only afterwards HTML-unescapes it via IE_sanitize(html.unescape(...)). Entity-encoded path separators therefore survive basename() and are decoded into real separators after the check, defeating the sanitization ordering.
exploit_scenario: POST multipart/form-data with Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="../../hax0rd.txt". basename() sees no separator; unescape() then yields '../../hax0rd.txt', which reaches the upload handler's new_file() as the file name.
preconditions: A file upload handler or view that uses the parsed file name to construct a filesystem path without further validation.
recommendation: HTML-unescape the filename first, then strip Windows-style separators, and apply os.path.basename() as the final step, in one sanitize_file_name() helper used at the single call site.
